notes: Every advertised OpenClaw gateway method is classified exactly once by its leading method group. 'implement' includes methods already present in Metiq and methods assigned to a future workstream; this file does not implement those methods.

groups.rationale: Core operator/runtime methods are part of the supported or planned Metiq control surface; gaps remain backlog rather than accepted incompatibilities.
Session lifecycle, collaboration, approvals, and protocol-v4 chat are the primary WS-A parity target.
Channel lifecycle, cron, approvals, and node/device management map to WS-A items A3 and A5-A8.
Memory diagnostics and migration controls align with the existing memory subsystem and WS-C lifecycle work.
Plugin approvals, package lifecycle, and skill curation belong to the WS-G platform/security roadmap.
Messaging and media methods extend existing channel, voice, and TTS capabilities rather than defining an incompatible product boundary.
OpenClaw durable local user profiles and email aliases differ from Metiq's Nostr-pubkey identity and event-derived profile model.
These methods are OpenClaw-branded editor/setup or Control UI integrations; Metiq exposes its own Web UI and migration surfaces instead.
Terminal PTY sessions, workspace-rooted fs.listDir, and the git worktree lifecycle are implemented as WS-native gateway surfaces in the A7 pass.
Board/conversation, attachment, artifact, MCP-app, environment, task-suggestion, and interactive-question surfaces remain deferred until their vertical slices land (WS-A/A7 follow-ups).

method_notes.chat.abort: Operator abort remains unconditional. Busy queue-mode interrupt is tool-aware: it aborts only when active tools are interruptible and otherwise defers newest input as urgent active-run steering.
method_notes.config.schema.lookup: Returns schema for a specific config path; full schema when path is empty.
